_comment: The fork targets Gecko 157+. This file is the machine-checked record of
which platform capabilities the code actually relies on, so a Chromium-
shaped assumption cannot creep back in behind a plausible comment.
capabilities = load-bearing: without it a feature is missing or wrong, and
shipsInFirefox is the floor the target must clear. hostProbes = the code
feature-detects and degrades when the host says no, with `why` naming what
is lost. The split is the point: a probe is not automatically safe, and a
new one has to be argued for rather than inherited.
tests/capabilities.test.mjs enforces it: declared grants must match the
userscript banner exactly, every usedBy/verifiedBy path must exist, no
capability may require a Firefox newer than the 157 floor, anything in
`retired` must not reappear in src/, every capability/hostProbe token must
really appear in the files it claims, and every `probes` chain the code
feature-detects must be classified in exactly one entry - so adopting a
new platform API cannot skip the manifest the way scheduler.postTask and

Known boundary of the scan: it reads `typeof` chains whose root is a global or a known host object. A member probe on a local reference (cue.getCueAsHTML, el.requestFullscreen) starts at a lowercase local name, and an unguarded bare global (new MediaMetadata) is not a typeof at all - neither is machine-visible. Those are recorded here by hand instead, and the token check keeps the rows honest too. The scan is a floor on coverage, not a ceiling.

injectionContext.why: Violentmonkey 2.49.0 runs a @grant-ed script in an isolated content realm, not the page world, which is the default for @inject-into auto once any @grant is present. That is why the banner pins no @sandbox / @inject-into: there is no directive that would give PF a page-realm global it needs, and it never reads one - SDK detection is selector-based against the composed DOM ancestry. The realm is unobservable to PF, and that was verified rather than assumed, on a real 2.49.0 build driving the shipped bundle: the kernel boots, finds a Plyr-anchored video, and adopts it into an open shadow root with an adopted stylesheet, while window.PlayerForge and the GM_* globals are absent from the page world. A cross-realm constructable stylesheet was the one integration point a realm change could plausibly break (src/shell/chrome/inject.js) and it works. Not inferred.

allFrames.why: The banner sets @allFrames true explicitly, but that line is INERT on the shipping target: 2.49.0 has no allFrames meta key at all - the string appears nowhere in the shipped XPI. It gates sub-frames with @noframes instead, and its script collector skips any script whose noframes flag is set, so PF reaches every frame by default. The line is kept only for a Tampermonkey user, whose Firefox build defaults sub-frame injection to true but whose Content Script mode also grants no real document_start.

capabilities.summary: UA-owned dismissal watcher for the settings panel: the UA closes the panel on Esc (and the Android back button) even when a page-level keydown handler swallows or reorders the event before it reaches the shadow host
capabilities.note: Enabled by default in Gecko 149 (bug 1966073), below the 157 floor, so the watcher in #armDismissal is the live dismissal path on every supported target and the guarded keydown/pointerdown document listeners are the fallback rather than the primary. The probe is kept because the constructor can still throw on a host that gates the interface; the catch degrades to the keydown path instead of failing.

capabilities.summary: One shared stylesheet, upgraded in place across shadow roots
Frame-clock sampling for the jank watchdog and resume timing
Interaction latency for the debug jank diagnostic: PerformanceObserver('event') with interactionId grouping, the one signal the rAF frame-gap watchdog structurally cannot see
capabilities.why: A slow event handler that still finishes inside its frame never moves the frame clock, so a 300ms click handler on a page holding 60fps reports as perfectly healthy today. Event Timing measures handler-to-paint latency directly. Debug-only and behind the same setDebugRuntime toggle as the rAF loop, so a user without debug pays zero.
capabilities.note: shipsInFirefox 102 is the first release with Event Timing; 157 was verified to list `event` in supportedEntryTypes (it does NOT list longtask or long-animation-frame, which is why the rAF watchdog stays). This is a supplement, never a replacement: Gecko ships no PerformanceScriptTiming, so entries carry no per-script attribution - we learn THAT an interaction was slow, never WHICH handler. Node has no `event` entry type at all, so the test harness drives a fake PerformanceObserver; without that fake these tests would stay green even if the install path broke.

capabilities.summary: Priority + delay + abort task scheduling behind every deferred path: removal grace, mutation-dispatch defer, lifecycle settle, context retry, resume throttle
capabilities.note: Called unconditionally on the 157 floor, so there is no probe to classify; the jsdom test host gets a timer-backed polyfill from tests/loader.mjs. scheduler.yield is deliberately not used; see the module header.

capabilities.summary: Native WebVTT parsing, cuechange scheduling at exact enter/exit boundaries, and VTTCue.getCueAsHTML() for spec-whitelisted cue markup
capabilities.note: The renderer never parses cue text: getCueAsHTML is why <b>/<i>/<c>/ruby survive as real nodes. 31 covers VTTCue, its geometry, and getCueAsHTML together; region support would be 59.

capabilities.summary: Rich OS media-surface metadata (title, artist, artwork) for the media session
capabilities.note: Constructed unguarded, so this is an implicit dependency: tests/loader.mjs shims MediaMetadata because no test host has it.

grants.why: Manager-scoped storage: readable from any @match origin, unlike a page origin's localStorage.
grants.managerShape: 2.49.0 reads the script's value table synchronously and hands stored values back as real objects, unwrapped from the JSON-tagged form. PF reads its whole config document through this during boot, so a promise-returning shape would deadlock the entry path.
2.49.0 updates the script's value table synchronously; PF reads back through GM_getValue against that same table and never confirms a commit with a write round-trip.

grants.why: Cross-tab notification for pf:configs - the one capability the page origin cannot provide.
grants.managerShape: 2.49.0 mints a FRESH id per call (`s || (s = x("VMvc"), n[s] = cb)`) into a per-key table and delivers to every registration, so each shell's ResumeStore keeps an independent id and unsubscribe with no fan-out of PF's own. This is the one shape that made a per-key fan-out look necessary under a previous target; it is not.

grants.why: Detaches the above; a grant without its remover cannot clean up.
grants.managerShape: Takes the id 2.49.0 minted, walking the per-key tables to find it. PF only ever calls it with a handle its matching add call returned, so the id is always valid.

2.49.0 clones its third argument, sets opts.text from the caption, keys the entry on `opts.id || caption` and RETURNS that key - so the options object is the correct type there and the handle is always usable, with no fallback needed.
Deletes by the key registerMenuCommand returned, so the pair is used symmetrically: PF stores the returned handle and hands it straight back.

grants.why: Manager-cached stylesheet warm-load, upgraded in place over the embedded sheet.
grants.managerShape: Present and resolved synchronously; verified callable in the content realm on 2.49.0, which is what the shell's stylesheet upgrade depends on.

grants.why: CORS-bypassing subtitle fetch from user-supplied hosts.
grants.managerShape: Callback-based with a numeric status and responseText on 2.49.0. Its @connect is parsed and stored but NOT enforced in MV2: a script declaring `@connect 127.0.0.2` still fetched 127.0.0.1 and got 200, and a dead-port `@connect 127.0.0.1:1` did the same, so it is neither host- nor port-matched. The banner's `@connect *` is therefore not what permits these fetches. Do not cite the native harness's api-gm.js here - it enforces a host allowlist, but it is the test double, not the manager.

retired.summary: The @grant for a manager's URL-change event
retired.why: Nothing in the fork subscribes to route changes: same-document navigation is out of scope, so there is no consumer to receive the event. Re-granting it would widen the permission surface for zero coverage.
Gecko does not implement LoAF. The rAF frame-gap watchdog in src/shared/diagnostics.js is the debug-only replacement.

Gecko exposes the method but not the behaviour: since 89 it has been a shim that returns an empty sequence for every UA-generated event (bug 1702175, 'getPredictedEvents can just return empty sequence normally'), and the real implementation (bug 1550461) is still open. So the typeof guard in the scrub path passed on the 157 floor while the call could never contribute a sample - it bought nothing and cost one array allocation on every non-zero pointer move in a path written to allocate nothing per move. Scrub velocity is measured from coalesced and live samples only.
Never called by any feature, so the grant would be dead permission surface. Use navigator.clipboard instead.

hostProbes.summary: Is there a document at all?
hostProbes.why: yield_() needs visibilityState to decide between a frame and a task. Node and worker hosts have no document, and both resolve on a MessageChannel task instead.

hostProbes.summary: Frame boundary for yield_() and the jank watchdog
hostProbes.why: Absent on Node/jsdom, where yield_ falls back to a MessageChannel task behind a 50ms backstop, so boot cannot stall on a host that never paints.

hostProbes.summary: Off-screen gate that stops media-clock writes for players the user cannot see
hostProbes.why: Without it the gate stays open, which is the safe direction: saves continue, nothing is lost.

hostProbes.summary: Compact-mode auto-detect and the panel breakpoint listener
hostProbes.why: jsdom has no viewport engine; matches is false, so the shell never auto-switches to compact and no listener fires.
Heads without a screen object skip the check rather than measuring against a bogus viewport.
A manager that does not provide it simply has no menu; the settings surface carries the same switch.
Missing remover is handled by no-op, so a teardown cannot throw on a manager without it.
Without it resume entries do not sync live between tabs; they still sync on next load.
A grant without its remover is exactly the case that leaks, so the remover is probed too and no-ops.
Absent, the injected stylesheet is adopted on its own; the warm path is an optimisation.

hostProbes.summary: Manager and script identity for the about/diagnostics surface
hostProbes.why: Deliberately unprobed and ungranted: the manager exposes GM_info to a script with no grants (true of both Tampermonkey MV2 and Violentmonkey MV2), so bare use is correct. Declared here so nobody 'fixes' it by adding a grant - the grant-equality test would then fail on a permission that buys nothing.

hostProbes.summary: Compositor-side accent flash and the transform transition
hostProbes.why: flashElement() returns early and the settings/toast flash is simply skipped, and the transform path falls back to its rAF setter - both are cosmetic, so no version floor is claimed.
hostProbes.note: Two guarded call sites, one degradation story: the first has no fallback (nothing flashes), the second has an rAF one. getAnimations()/effect.getKeyframes() are optional-chained or typeof-guarded inside the same pass.

hostProbes.summary: Skips a parked video whose opacity or visibility is already collapsed
hostProbes.why: Falls through to the rect-only path below it, so the candidate scan still works; only the cheap reject is lost.

hostProbes.summary: Full-rate pointer sampling for the forge scrub gesture
hostProbes.why: The single event's coordinates are used instead, so a fast drag samples less densely - the gesture stays correct, just coarser.

hostProbes.summary: The document-wide fullscreen gate, its transition events, and the exit call
hostProbes.why: The gate is driven by fullscreenchange and only latches from a real fullscreenElement, so a host without the API never sets fs and document.exitFullscreen() is unreachable; entering degrades to the blocked-embed hint.
hostProbes.note: Not machine-visible: entry is a requestFullscreen() on a local element reference, exit is guarded by the fs value rather than a typeof.
